Exercise A

Uluru and the Outback

Read the text and choose the word that fits each gap. The bold verbs show you the past perfect at work.

Before you read — optional, not marked
This is just to get you thinking — you can leave it empty and it does not count towards your score.
Reading text

Uluru is a sandstone rock that rises 348 metres out of the flat red 1 in the middle of Australia. By the time the first European explorers reached it in 1873, the Anangu people had lived in this landscape for more than 30,000 years. For them the rock was never a tourist 2 — it was, and still is, a sacred place.

The explorer William Gosse gave the rock an English name, but he did not know that it had carried the name Uluru for thousands of years already. The land itself was given back to its traditional 3 in 1985, and eight years later both names became 4 together.

Life in the Outback is hard. Temperatures can 5 45°C in summer, and the nearest town may be four hours away by car. Farmers who had waited months for rain sometimes lose everything in a single 6. Children on remote sheep stations study with the School of the Air, a radio and internet school that has taught families in the bush since 1951.

Today about 300,000 people visit Uluru every year. Since 2019 nobody is 7 to climb the rock, because the Anangu had asked visitors for decades to respect their 8 and stay on the ground.

Exercise D

Writing: One Day in the Outback

You have spent a week in the Outback with your exchange class. Write a diary entry of 6–8 sentences for the class blog that your exchange partner in Adelaide will read, saying what you did on one day and what had happened before it. Use at least three past perfect forms.

Ideas you can use

• The bus left at five in the morning — nobody had slept much.

• By the time you arrived, the guide had already made breakfast.

• Somebody had forgotten their water bottle.

• You saw the rock change colour after the sun had gone down.

You can use these: By the time we... After we had... Before that,... As soon as... I had never ... before. It was the first time I had...
Your diary entry
Aim for 6–8 sentences with at least three past perfect forms.
